title: Veterans’ Affairs Legislation Amendment (Military Compensation Review and Other Measures) Bill 2013

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would change military rehabilitation, compensation and treatment arrangements, including support for dependants, pension eligibility and the administration of payments under veterans' legislation.

It would assess impairment payment dates by individual accepted condition, expand partner lump sum choices, increase eligible children's periodic compensation and expand financial and legal advice assistance for eligible members and wholly dependent partners.
Measures would also cover serving and former members, specified partners and dependants, with changes to reviews, treatment access, superannuation offsets and payment administration.
changes: Rehabilitation responsibilities assigned to Service Chiefs would transfer to the Chief of the Defence Force, with delegation powers.
The Veterans' Review Board could remit matters for needs assessment and compensation.
Special Rate Disability Pension eligibility would expand for otherwise eligible people with lump sum incapacity payments or payments fully offset by Commonwealth superannuation.
Specified defence-related claimants under the Safety, Rehabilitation and Compensation Act would receive treatment cards for accepted service injuries.
Travelling expense entitlements would extend to partners of specified eligible people in defined circumstances.
Overpayments under military compensation legislation could be recovered from Veterans' Entitlements Act payments.
summary.affected: Serving and former Defence Force members, eligible partners and children would be affected.

speeches.speaker: Anne McEwen
speeches.brief: The speaker moved to extend the reporting deadline for the Export Finance and Insurance Corporation Amendment (New Mandate and Other Measures) Bill 2013 and the Veterans' Affairs Legislation Amendment (Military Compensation Review and Other Measures) Bill 2013 to 17 June 2013, and the motion was agreed to.

speeches.speaker: Jane Prentice
speeches.brief: Explained the bill implements Campbell review recommendations worth over $39 million with a net Commonwealth cost of $17.4 million, welcomed the extension of non-liability mental health care for veterans from 1 July next year, and recalled that Labor and the Greens voted down the coalition's fair indexation legislation on 16 June 2011, which she called a day of disgrace.

speeches.speaker: Michael McCormack
speeches.brief: Supported the Veterans' Affairs Legislation Amendment (Military Compensation Review and Other Measures) Bill 2013, which implements recommendations from the military compensation review, noting $25 million for veterans' health services, a net cost of $17.4 million, and a total reform cost of $39.6 million offset by $22 million in savings; urged fair indexation of DFRB and DFRDB entitlements.

speeches.speaker: Michael Ronaldson
speeches.brief: The government was condemned for allowing only four minutes to debate comprehensive changes to the Military Rehabilitation and Compensation Act 2004. The coalition supported the bill but opposed Senator Xenophon's amendments to impose legislated 120-day processing time limits for compensation claims.
